title: libnetwork/etchosts: fix host IP resolution in WSL mirrored networking mode
body:
Fixes host.containers.internal resolution in WSL2 with mirrored networking mode (networkingMode=Mirrored).

### Problem
In WSL2 with mirrored networking mode, Linux shares network interfaces and IPs with the Windows host.
The default route gateway (r.Gw) points to the external LAN router (e.g. 192.168.5.1), not the Windows host.
Resolving host.containers.internal to r.Gw sends container traffic to the external router interface rather than the Windows host, causing subsequent Windows bind() calls on the same port to fail with WSAEADDRINUSE / WinError 10013.

### Solution
1. Detect mirrored networking mode via wslinfo --networking-mode (checking PATH and fallback /usr/sbin/wslinfo).
2. When mirrored mode is detected, ask the kernel routing table (netlink.RouteGet) for the preferred source IP (routes[0].Src) used to reach the default gateway, which corresponds to the Windows host's mirrored IP.
3. Fall back to the first global unicast IPv4 address assigned to the default route's network interface.
4. If no valid host IP can be resolved in mirrored mode, return empty string rather than the router gateway to avoid port conflicts.
5. Preserve default gateway resolution in WSL NAT mode.
